# Atmospheric Network Monitor An atmospheric network monitor is a computer that displays information about the station's monitored [textlink="pipe networks" link="PipeNetworks"].
It is a useful tool for quickly assessing the temperature, pressure, and gas composition of the station's [textlink="pipe networks" link="PipeNetworks"], as well as their routes through the station.
## Network List The atmospheric network monitor displays a list of all the station's monitored [textlink="pipe networks" link="PipeNetworks"].
Each network takes its name and color from the gas pipe sensor monitoring it. To change a network's name or color, rename it with a labeler or repaint it with a spray painter.
Clicking a network will display detailed information about it and highlight its route on the station map.
This information includes the total amount of gas in the network in moles, as well as its gas composition. This is extremely useful for monitoring important networks such as Distro, which cannot operate properly below certain pressures.
## Station Map The atmospheric network monitor displays the location of every [textlink="pipe network" link="PipeNetworks"] on the station map, along with all pipe devices. Note that a pipe network does not need a gas pipe sensor connected to it to appear on the map.
These devices appear on the map in the same color they have on the station. This helps distinguish individual [textlink="pipe networks" link="PipeNetworks"] and their connected devices.
Pipe devices are grouped in the map legend by function: - [bold]Network Opening[/bold] - a device that connects a pipe network to the station atmosphere, such as [textlink="air vents" link="AirVents"], [textlink="passive vents" link="PassiveVent"], and [textlink="air injectors" link="AirInjector"]. - [bold]Air Scrubber[/bold] - simply an [textlink="air scrubber" link="AirScrubber"]. - [bold]Flow Regulator[/bold] - a device that controls gas flow through a pipe network, such as [textlink="gas pumps" link="Pumps"], [textlink="gas valves" link="Valves"], and [textlink="gas mixers/filters" link="MixingAndFiltering"]. The arrow on the device shows the direction of gas flow. This also often determines where a pipe network is separated or split. - [bold]Thermoregulator[/bold] - any device that affects the temperature of gas in a pipe network, such as [textlink="thermomachines" link="Thermomachines"], [textlink="radiators" link="Radiators"], and even medical cryopods.
## Gas Pipe Sensors Atmospheric network monitors collect data about [textlink="pipe networks" link="PipeNetworks"] through gas pipe sensors.
By default, the station should have gas pipe sensors on every major [textlink="pipe network" link="PipeNetworks"], such as the Distro and Waste networks.
If you want to monitor a new network, build a gas pipe sensor and it will automatically appear on the atmospheric network monitor. Make sure you build the sensor on the pipe network you want to monitor. [textlink="Pipe networks" link="PipeNetworks"] are easily separated by a simple gas pump or valve, which can cause the sensor to display data from an entirely different network.
